title: Model pinning, routing and compatibility: edge cases & operational matrix (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note to capture subtle interactions between model registry version-pinning and the request routing/control plane across multi-region and multi-capacity deployments. Aim: enumerate edge cases, produce a compact compatibility matrix, and propose deterministic policies that avoid silent behavior changes for customers when pins + routing rules collide.

Background / context:
- Registry supports: model families, named versions (v1, v1.1, v2-rc), and variant tags (cpu-quant, gpu-amp).
- Routing supports policy layers: customer-level pin (explicit version), tenant route rules (region preferences), capacity tiers (dedicated vs hosted fallback), and emergency fallback policies.
- Problem: when a request is pinned to a specific model version that is incompatible with available runtime kernel/quant profile in the chosen region or tier, the router must decide between failing, falling back to a compatible variant, or rerouting to a different region/capacity. We need deterministic, observable, and safe behavior.

Definitions / terms used here:
- Pin: explicit model version identifier supplied by customer or tenant config (e.g., my-model@v1.2).
- Variant: runtime-optimized build of the same version (e.g., v1.2-cpu-8bit, v1.2-gpu-fp16).
- Compatible runtime: a runtime image and kernel set that can load and serve the model variant without producing silent correctness regressions.
- Strict pin: an option where router must return an error if exact pinned artifact is not available.

Assumptions:
- Registry records artifact metadata: architecture, quantization format, required runtime kernels, minimal driver versions, and region availability table.
- Router has read-only, cached copy of registry metadata (TTL ~30s).
- Router can query capacity inventory per region/tier synchronously (fast path) or use cached snapshot.
- Customers expect pinned versions to be stable; silent substitution is unacceptable unless explicitly enabled.

Compatibility matrix (compact, human-readable):
Columns: model_version | declared_variants | runtime_kernels_required | typical_locations | pin_behavior_default | fallback_allowed | fallback_target | notes
- my-model@v1.0 | gpu-fp16, cpu-8bit | kernel-v3 (attn-v2) | us-west-1 (dedicated), eu-west-1 (hosted) | honor-pin -> allow variant-substitution | yes (if variant compatible) | v1.0-cpu-8bit or region failover | if pinned explicitly by user, prefer error unless user allowed_variant_subs=true
- my-model@v1.1-quant | cpu-4bit | kernel-v4 (quant-support) | hosted-only (us-east-1) | honor-pin -> strict by default | no | none (error) | 4-bit artifacts are fragile; do not auto-fallback to 8-bit
- my-model@v2-rc | gpu-amp, kernel-v5 | kernel-v5 | dedicated-only (apac) | honor-pin -> can reroute regionally | yes (reroute) | v2-rc-gpu-amp @ apac -> reroute to apac dedicated | network latency warning to customer; require explicit opt-in for reroute across continents
- base-embed@2024-09 | cpu-int8 | kernel-v2 | global hosted | honor-pin -> soft | yes | nearest region with cpu-int8 | embeddings less sensitive; safe to fallback to nearest compatible region

Notes on the table: this is intentionally conservative. Key decisions encoded:
- If pinned artifact has multiple declared variants, substitution across variants MAY be allowed only when attribute-compat (same model weights + different quant format declared-compatible) and customer has not opted into strict-pin.
- If pinned artifact is unique (only one declared variant), router should fail fast and surface clear error message with suggested remediation: list of available variants, or offer to reroute.

Edge cases (real incidents we've seen or could see):
1) Pin to version that depends on a kernel not yet deployed in region (race between rollout and pin). Result: silent fallback to older kernel leading to TTI regressions.
2) Pin to a quantized artifact (4-bit), router falls back to 8-bit variant and returns subtly different logits (customer didn't expect).
3) Pin + tenant-level canary route that pins to a model variant not available in the canary region; router chooses global fallback causing canary metrics to be polluted.
4) Multi-region failover: pinned version exists only in a private dedicated pool in region A; in region B only hosted compatible variant exists. Router reroutes across region causing data residency violation.
5) Rolling deprecation: registry marks v1.0 deprecated and removes auto-compat flags — pinned customers should keep serving, but routing and capacity reclamation causes 504s.

Proposed control-plane / routing policy (deterministic rules):
A) Priority order when handling a request with an explicit pin (algo):
  1) Validate registry metadata for exact artifact availability in target route (region + tier).
  2) If exact artifact available -> serve.
  3) If exact artifact unavailable -> check: (a) customer strict-pin flag? if true -> return 412 with payload explaining availability and remediation.
  4) If strict-pin=false -> check declared variant compatibility set. If variants exist and compatible_with_target_runtime -> select highest-preference variant following preference order: same-region same-tier > same-region fallback-tier > cross-region same-tier (only if cross-region_allowed_by_customer).
  5) If no compatible variant -> apply fallback policy: either fail (default) or if emergency-fallback enabled by tenant -> route to designated global fallback model (must be registered as fallback in registry with explicit consent).

B) Metadata requirements the registry must expose to the control plane:
- variant_ids (list)
- declared_compatibility_tags (list, e.g., "same-weights-different-quant-allowed")
- required_kernel_version
- supported_hardware (e.g., a100, gpus-family-x, cpu-avx512)
- allowed_cross_region_failover boolean
- data_residency_label (to enforce legal constraints)
- deprecation_status and deprecation_end_date

C) Router invariants (runtime checks):
- Never auto-promote an artifact from a different model name even if weights appear similar.
- If do-reroute across region -> emit high-cardinality event with reason, latency delta estimate, and customer-visible header X-Redwood-Routed-From.
- Count substitution events as a distinct metric and surface in the Console as a routed-substitution alert.

API contract clarifications (for SDK and public API):
- New optional fields: strict_pin (bool), allow_variant_subs (bool), allow_cross_region_reroute (bool). Default: strict_pin=false, allow_variant_subs=false, allow_cross_region_reroute=false.
- Error schema must include: reason_code (PIN_UNAVAILABLE | INCOMPATIBLE_RUNTIME | DATA_RESIDENCY_BLOCKED), available_alternatives (list of variant ids or regions), suggested_action.

Rollout and migration notes:
- Backfill registry metadata for all models before enabling variant-substitution. Poor metadata leads to bad fallbacks.
- Feature gate: start with substitution disabled; enable allow_variant_subs at tenant opt-in level and observe metrics for 2 weeks.
- Add a "pin-preservation" job for Dedicated reclaim flows: do not evict pinned artifacts until tenants migrate or until explicit deprecation window.

Testing checklist (pre-prod):
- Unit tests for router decision tree covering all permutations of flags.
- Integration tests: fake registry with mixed availability, ensure correct error codes and metric emissions.
- Chaos test: simulate a region losing kernel-v3 and confirm strict-pinned requests fail but soft-pinned requests follow deterministic fallback path.
- Data residency test: ensure cross-region reroute is blocked when data_residency_label mismatch.

Observability & Alerts:
- Metrics to emit: pin_request_count, pin_substitution_count, pin_error_count_by_reason, pin_reroute_latency_delta.
- Console: a per-tenant view showing recent substituted requests (with example input/response diffs for sampling).
- Alerting: if substitution rate > 0.5% of total pinned requests for a tenant over 1h -> page on-call infra.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should we allow variant substitution for safety-critical customers even if they asked for strict-pin? (probably not; strict semantics should be honored)
- Cross-region reroute: default off for privacy/regulatory reasons, but we should define a fast opt-in path for customers that value availability over locality.
- Operational complexity: how much of the decision tree belongs in the router vs a policy service? (favored: thin router enforces simple checks + policy-service that returns recommended action).

Action items (owners):
- Inventory: backfill required_kernel_version and declared_compatibility_tags for all artifacts. Owner: Anita Bose, due 2025-02-18.
- API: add three pin-related fields to public API and SDK. Owner: Diego Morales, PR draft by 2025-02-01.
- Policy service spike: design a small policy decision service that returns {action, reason, chosen_variant, metrics_tags}. Owner: Priya Nair, spike by 2025-01-24.
- UX: Console change to surface substitutions and allow tenant opt-in toggles. Owner: product-hosted-api (TBD)

Appendix: Example error payload (stringified)
- 412 PIN_UNAVAILABLE -> {
    "reason_code": "PIN_UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "Pinned artifact my-model@v1.1-quant not available in target region/us-west-1",
    "available_alternatives": ["v1.1-cpu-8bit@us-east-1"],
    "suggested_action": "Set allow_variant_subs=true or deploy artifact to region"
  }

This doc is intentionally a sketch. Follow-ups: map this to the registry schema PR, update router integration tests, and schedule a platform review with SRE and legal for cross-region data residency edge cases.
